items.summary: The Devils announced Sunday that Connor Hellebuyck will not start in his return to Winnipeg on Tuesday.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con The New Jersey Devils made waves on Sunday night when, following their 4-0 win over the Toronto Maple Leafs , they announced that newly acquired star goalie Connor Hellebuyck would not start in his first game back in Manitoba against the Winnipeg Jets on Tuesday. The Devils’ statement, which cited a “reduction in our expected win probability” that would come along with Hellebuyck starting, has drawn the ire of fans and commentators alike. New Jersey’s decision to keep Hellebuyck out of that game will spare him from the boos and chants of Winnipeg fans just a few weeks after star winger Brady Tkachuk, now with the Florida Panthers , was jeered heavily in his return to Canada’s capital against the Ottawa Senators . Hellebuyck has been excellent for his new team since he was dealt in October. In five appearances, he has gone 5-0-0 with a .913 save percentage and 1.96 goals against average along with a shutout. items.title: Former NHLer Bobby Sheehan passes away at 77
items.summary: Sheehan was a member of the Montreal Canadiens’ 1971 Stanley Cup championship team.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources The hockey world has lost a member of the Montreal Canadiens ‘ 1971 Stanley Cup championship team. On Monday, the NHL Alumni Association announced that former center Bobby Sheehan passed away at the age of 77. The Weymouth, Massachusetts native was selected by the Canadiens out of the Ontario Hockey Association’s St. Catherines Black Hawks in the 1969 NHL Amateur Draft. He spent his first two professional seasons in Montreal’s organization, playing 45 total regular season games with the Canadiens and winning the Stanley Cup with Montreal in 1971. Sheehan joined the California Golden Seals for the 1971-72 season, where he scored 20 goals and added 26 assists for 46 points in 78 games. Following his lone season with the Golden Seals, Sheehan had a three-year stint in the World Hockey Association (WHA). His 1972-73 season with the WHA’s New York Raiders was the best of his career, putting up 35 goals and 53 assists for 88 points in 75 games. He stayed with New York (which would be renamed the New York Golden Blades and then the Jersey Knights) for most of the 1973-74 season before moving on to the Edmonton Oilers through the 1974-75 season. Sheehan returned to the NHL with the Chicago Black Hawks in the 1975-76 season, and then played for the Detroit Red Wings in the 1976-77 season. He went back to the WHA for one last season in 1977-78, when played for the Indianapolis Racers. Sheehan then spent the rest of his career splitting time between the New York Rangers , Colorado Rockies, and Los Angeles Kings of the NHL, the New Haven Nighthawks and Binghamton Whalers of the American Hockey League (AHL), and the Forth Worth Texans of the Central Hockey League (CHL), before retiring in 1983. items.title: Spotlight on Flames defenceman Nemec after Bahl injury
items.summary: After the Flames lost Kevin Bahl to injury, the interesting part became who would step up. His partner, Simon Nemec, now has an opportunity, writes Eric Francis.
items.body: CALGARY - The Calgary Flames have lost their best defenceman, their most reliable matchup player and, according to head coach Ryan Huska, their best player through the opening portion of the season. Kevin Bahl’s season-ending Achilles injury is a harsh blow to a rebuilding team trying to remain competitive and establish some consistency in a season that figures to have its share of growing pains. The Flames immediately addressed the loss of the six-foot-six lefty by replacing him on the top pairing the last two games with 35-year-old Joel Hanley. But the spotlight is now squarely on his partner, Simon Nemec . We're about to find out a whole lot more about the 22-year-old former second overall pick who arrived in Calgary this summer for two first round picks and a second. The price tag suggests he’ll be one of the organization's foundational pieces. Now we’ll pay even more attention to how he’s progressing towards that status. He’s been thrust into an even more pressure-packed situation — the kind he insisted he wanted so badly in Jersey. He insists there was already plenty of pressure, given the five-year, $36 million deal he signed this summer. But he won't be able to lean on Bahl like he has so far. “I feel like we were probably the perfect pair, if you see the size, the hands, and the style of hockey, so that is probably is gonna change a little bit,” said Nemec. “He's the reason why my game has been growing up, but I don't want to say it was just because of him. I think I'm playing pretty good hockey.” So far, his first season in Calgary has been something of a quiet audition. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect An eventful year in the life of goaltender Remi Poirier continues. The league announced that the Dallas Stars claimed Poirier off waivers on Monday after he was placed on the wire on Sunday by the Washington Capitals . Poirier, 25, now returns to the organization that drafted him and with which he began this season before a series of transactions. The Stars waived him at the end of training camp and the preseason with the intent to assign him to their AHL affiliate Texas Stars, but he was claimed by the New Jersey Devils, who had considerable organizational need for goaltending depth at the time. The Devils then landed super star workhorse Connor Hellebuyck in a blockbuster trade, and shortly thereafter sent Poirier to the Capitals in exchange for a seventh-round pick in the 2027 NHL Draft. Now, he returns to the Stars, who chose him with the No. 185 overall selection in the sixth round of the 2020 draft. The Quebec native turned pro after wrapping up his major junior career with the Gatineau Olympiques of the QMJHL in 2021-22. Poirier has yet to appear in a game at the NHL or AHL level this season. items.title: Arniel criticizes Devils’ decision not to play Hellebuyck vs. Jets: Goalie ‘gave up on us’
items.summary: The Winnipeg Jets aren’t too happy with the New Jersey Devils’ decision to bench Connor Hellebuyck in his return to Manitoba.
items.body: The Winnipeg Jets aren't too happy with the New Jersey Devils ' decision to bench Connor Hellebuyck in his return to Manitoba. Head coach Scott Arniel bashed the decision on Monday, citing a lack of closure for fans and teammates. "We've seen some other players go back to their buildings and do it and get it over and done with," Arniel said. "I know it's their decision and they can do whatever they want, but I think that it would put closure (to the situation). This doesn't. We're gonna see them in (nine) games in their building and I'm sure he's going to be in the net then. "To me, it goes back to the ownership, it goes back to the fans, it goes back to the core guys that have been with Helle from the very beginning that he kind of left on. ... He just gave up on us. It would be nice to finally be done with this," Arniel added. "I can feel the frustration of the fans. We wanted to get this put to bed. That’s the biggest thing. Now it’s not getting put to bed here. It’s going to linger again." The Devils announced on Sunday night that Hellebuyck would not play against his former team, with general manager Sunny Mehta citing a "reduction in our expected win probability" as the reasoning. “I’m disappointed, but I understand. When speaking to the media, Columbus Blue Jackets head coach Rick Bowness announced that forward Conor Garland will not be in the lineup on Tuesday night, when the Blue Jackets take on the Florida Panthers . Bowness said Garland is battling back from an upper-body injury but didn’t provide a timeline for his return. It isn’t quite clear when or where Garland was hurt. He played the entirety of Columbus’ last contest, a 5-2 loss to the Buffalo Sabres this past Friday night. The 30-year-old was a -2 while logging a little over 13 minutes of ice time, not too far from his average for the year. Garland had appeared in each of the Jackets’ first 15 games of the 2026-27 season, but has definitely looked far from the offensive threat he was earlier in his career. He has just one assist to his name to go along with his plus/minus of -5 while averaging 13:33 of ice time per game. This is the Scituate, Mass. native’s first full season in Columbus. The 20-year-old is in his first full AHL season, after joining the Marlies for the 2026 playoffs en route to a Calder Cup. He finished his OHL career last season, after four years split between the Oshawa Generals and Brantford Bulldogs. Danford totalled 99 points in 233 OHL regular-season games and 19 points in 60 playoff contests. The Maple Leafs' No. 31 overall pick in the 2024 NHL Draft had a goal and two assists during the Marlies' playoff run last year, but has taken on a much bigger role this year. items.body: Aho, Kotkaniemi played underground inside Veikkaus Arena during junior hockey careers HELSINKI -- The awe helped beat the jet lag when the Carolina Hurricanes showed up for their first practice at Veikkaus Arena on Monday in preparation for the 2026 NHL Global Series against the Seattle Kraken later this week.​ The Hurricanes trudged into the rink about two hours after landing, the end of an eight-hour overnight flight. Getting a sweat and working the legs are important in beating jet lag, but it's not always fun. This time, though, was different, in part because of the setting. The Hurricanes used the arena's practice rink, known as "The Cave," for a brisk afternoon practice. The rink is two stories underground, carved out of the bedrock upon which the arena is built. The white stone walls and roof contribute to an intimate setting. It's home to the junior team of Jokerit, one of the biggest clubs in Liiga, the top-tier professional league in Finland. We are now 41 days into the fantasy season and are witnessing teams start to separate in our league standings. It’s a long season, but we are nearing the quarter-mark. On the other side of the coin, four teams failed to pick up a win as Chicago (4), San Jose (4), Vancouver (3) and Toronto (3) went without a win in Week 6. Luckily for him, they were not being directed at the New Jersey Devils goalie — but rather towards the Toronto Maple Leafs , who were jeered by the home crowd after losing for the fifth time in six games. For Hellebuyck, the echoes of boos were supposed to be a small taste of things to come for his highly-anticipated return to Winnipeg on Tuesday. Now he might not even hear them More Videos Following Sunday's win against Toronto, the Devils announced that the 33-year-old would not be starting against the Winnipeg Jets , with GM Sunny Mehta citing a "reduction in our expected win probability" as the primary reason he will sit out. Winnipeg fans, of course, will cite another reason: he's scared to face the fanbase. "I love Winnipeg and playing there again — and just facing the music and seeing the reaction — would have been nice," said Hellebuyck. "It's out of my hands." items.title: Canadiens’ Arber Xhekaj finding comfort zone in depth role
items.summary: Arber Xhekaj has been providing more evidence of just how comfortable he’s become in the role he had so much trouble nailing down last season. Eric Engels has the story.
items.body: BROSSARD, Que. — There was a sequence in last Tuesday’s game against the Winnipeg Jets that was perfectly indicative of Arber Xhekaj ’s improvement this season, and it came long before he threw his last right-hand cross at Tyrel Bauer’s head. It was in the ninth minute of the second period when Xhekaj set up a great one-timer opportunity in the offensive zone for Adam Engstrom and then hustled back into position in his own end to simultaneously deny a zone entry and a hit from Viggo Bjorck. In both instances, Xhekaj steadied himself, chose the play he was going to make before the puck arrived, and executed to perfection. The pass to Engstrom was the best of several decisions Xhekaj could’ve made in that situation, and it led to a quality scoring chance. And everything he did immediately after that led to the Canadiens continuing one of their only good sequences of the game — and led Bjorck back to the Jets’ bench worse for wear after bearing the brunt of a collision he initiated. That had to feel good for Xhekaj, who was one of roughly five Canadiens who didn’t need a hard look in the mirror after that history-making loss. He was as effective in that game as he had been in each of the 13 games he’d appeared in before it this season, and he’s been just as good since, providing more evidence of just how comfortable he’s become in the role he had so much trouble nailing down last season. items.title: Ducks’ Cutter Gauthier becomes first NHLer with three hat-tricks in a 10-day span to start a month
items.summary: The Swedish-born American set unique history and ranks third in the NHL with 15 goals through 17 games.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Anaheim Ducks forward Cutter Gauthier is enjoying himself this season and making history as the Ducks establish themselves as one of the NHL’s most thrilling teams through the first quarter of the 2026-27 regular season. On Sunday night, with a three-goal, one-assist performance in a 5-2 win over the Pittsburgh Penguins , he became the first player in NHL history to score three hat tricks within the first 10 days of a calendar month. Gauthier leaned on an empty-net goal in the final minute to earn himself the historic honor, as the Ducks became the first team since the 1988-90 LA Kings to score at least five goals in eight consecutive games. The 22-year-old started the month in peak form, scoring his first November hat trick on Nov. 1 in a 6-3 win over the Ottawa Senators . Two days later, he potted another trio against the struggling Vancouver Canucks in a 5-4 victory. Both of his first two hat-tricks in November included two power-play goals, as he makes the most of Anaheim’s league-leading 38.5 percent success rate on the man advantage this season. Yet, his history-making performance against the Penguins didn’t need any special-teams help, with two goals coming at five-on-five before he netted the empty-net marker to seal the victory. Through 17 games this season, the Swedish-born American has 15 goals, good for third in the NHL, and seven assists for 22 points, ranking him 17th in NHL scoring overall. In his career, he has 76 goals and 60 assists for 136 points in 176 games with the Ducks and, previously, the Philadelphia Flyers . After Sunday’s win, the Ducks sit third in the Pacific Division with 21 points through the first 18 games of the 84-game campaign, as they look ahead to a Wednesday night home game against the Nashville Predators.

Then came the news that top-line winger Jack Roslovic, who’s been working through a nagging injury all week, was unable to go. items.summary: When Joel Farabee arrived in Calgary, he needed help figuring out how best to contribute. Now he wears an A and has added an offensive layer that has made him the Flames’ best and most productive forward this season.

On Sunday, the joke was on Philly, as Farabee’s third-period goal against his former club proved a pivotal moment in a 4-3 Flames win in which the hosts clawed back from three deficits to win in overtime. The irony was rich, as the goal came while he was killing a penalty. “Listen, especially that last year in Philly, I wasn't playing well enough to earn any more ice time than I got anyway, so I'm just very grateful for the opportunity I've gotten here,” he smiled. “I feel like I've played it my whole life, and I feel like it helps my game — it gets me involved in the game.” He’s not only involved this year, he has been the Flames’ best forward. items.title: Jets’ Brayden Yager savours first NHL goal: ‘Dream come true
items.body: WINNIPEG — Brayden Yager was grinning ear to ear while surrounded by reporters following a roller-coaster Sunday night at Canada Life Centre. The 21-year-old Winnipeg forward had just notched his first NHL goal — which was also his first NHL point — to help lift the Jets to an eventful 4-3 victory over the Tampa Bay Lightning. What made the milestone extra special was the small family cheering section sitting rinkside that shared in the meaningful moment. “Mom, dad and grandpa were here, so it was pretty cool to do it in front of them," Yager said after the game, still dripping with sweat. "Unbelievable feeling. Dream come true.” The Saskatchewan native's memorable moment was born out of a bloody sequence early in the third period. Winnipeg (7-8-3) was already protecting a 2-0 lead on second-period goals from Cole Perfetti and Morgan Barron when Lightning forward Pontus Holmberg caught Yager in the mouth with a high stick. The infraction drew blood, resulting in a four-minute double-minor penalty and a quick check-in with the team's medical staff. Yager was back on the ice moments later. With nine seconds remaining in the first minor, he fired a one-timer past Tampa Bay goaltender Andrei Vasilevskiy after a slick deflected feed from fellow rookie Viggo Bjorck. "Just a great play by Viggo there that touched over to me and I had a pretty wide-open net," Yager said. "You can definitely feel it, the atmosphere. I thought the fans were unbelievable tonight." Bjorck, selected eighth overall by Winnipeg in June's draft, collected his third assist in two games after enduring a 16-game scoring drought to begin his rookie campaign. Islanders defenseman Adam Pelech high-sticked Mantha in the throat with 7:25 remaining in the third period. Mantha took only one more shift before leaving the game. Now, Devils head coach Sheldon Keefe has revealed that Mantha has headed back to New Jersey for further evaluation and will be out of the club’s lineup for an undisclosed amount of time. “There’s some damage done there that they gotta get looked at and assess,” Keefe told the Devils’ Sam Kasan . “He is gonna miss some time. We just don’t know the extent of it at this point.” Pelech was assessed a two-minute minor penalty for high-sticking on the play. The game also featured a second-period semi-brawl in which Matthew Schaefer and Luke Hughes threw haymakers at one another behind New York’s net . The Devils scored the game-tying goal with Pelech in the box and ultimately won in overtime on a Jack Hughes breakaway. items.body: Register Login Panthers Recall Jack Devine By Brian La Rose | at November 8, 2026 6:46 pm Prior to their game against Boston this afternoon, the Panthers added some extra depth to their forward group. The team announced that they’ve recalled winger Jack Devine from AHL Charlotte. The 23-year-old was a seventh-round pick back in 2021, going 221st overall in 2022 and has clearly outperformed that draft selection. After a strong four seasons at the University of Denver (including tallying 56 and 57 points in his final two years), Devine turned pro last season, playing predominantly with the Checkers. items.body: It appears the Chicago Blackhawks are staying the course amid some choppy waters. Jeff Blashill will remain as Blackhawks' head coach as the team has opted not to make a coaching change, The Athletic 's Scott Powers reported on Sunday. The Blackhawks, in a rebuild for the better part of a decade, were intending this to be a season in which they turned a corner. Instead, they've started the year 4-13-1 — better only than the lowly Vancouver Canucks in the Western Conference. Things hit a low point with a 9-2 loss to the Carolina Hurricanes on Saturday night. The Blackhawks were off Sunday and don't play again until Thursday, which led many to wonder whether regime change is imminent. Instead, it appears general manager Kyle Davidson is giving Blashill some more time to right the ship. The former Detroit Red Wings coach was hired by Chicago ahead of the 2025-26 season. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images A couple of netminders have hit the wire. On Sunday, the Chicago Blackhawks placed goaltender Arvid Soderblom on waivers, with the Washington Capitals doing the same with fellow backstop Remi Poirier. Soderblom entered the 2026-27 season set to be the backup to Spencer Knight once again. However, while the Blackhawks have struggled as a whole, Soderblom’s play has been anything but up to par. In five appearances so far, four starts, the 27-year-old has allowed 21 goals, giving him a 4.67 goals-against average and a .842 save percentage, along with a 0-3-1 record. Who the Hawks would call up to take his place is yet to be determined. Drew Commesso has been with the organization the longest, having played a couple of games with Chicago on top of his time with the AHL’s Rockford IceHogs, but Stanislav Berezhnoy has had better numbers early on this year with Rockford. In 117 NHL games, Soderblom has a record of 25-68-15, with a 3.65 GAA, a .885 SV% and one shutout. He’s in the final season of his two-year contract extension, which he signed in July 2025. The deal carries an AAV of $2.75 million. Poirier was acquired by the Capitals last Sunday in exchange for a seventh-round pick from the New Jersey Devils , as the Devils had to make some roster moves after receiving Connor Hellebuyck from the Winnipeg Jets . Poirier, who was claimed off waivers by the Devils from the Dallas Stars , has yet to play a game this season. He has spent the past three seasons with the Stars’ top farm team, the Texas Stars. In 137 regular-season games in the AHL, the 25-year-old is 70-51-16, with a 2.76 GAA, a .908 SV% and six shutouts. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources The action is heating up in Denmark. The third day of the 2026 IIHF Women’s World Championship saw teams clinch spots in the quarterfinals, while other nations are found grasping at straws as they look to keep their knockout stage hopes alive. Which players stood out on Sunday? Let’s look back at what happened on a busy end to the first weekend of the tournament: The defending Olympic champions continued their strong start in the tournament with another convincing effort. Against the Germans, who were facing the U.S. in group play for the first time since 2008, the Americans faced an early assault, as they peppered goaltender Sandra Abstreiter with 18 shots in the first period. Once Casey O’Brien scored her second of the tournament in the latter half of the first period, the dam seemed to burst. Team USA’s attack overwhelmed Germany’s back end, and the way they maintained possession made it difficult for Trager der Adler to do anything. Defender Emma Peschel scored her first goal at the WWC in the final minute of the first period, before Alex Carpenter potted her first of the tournament in the second. Youngsters Abbey Murphy and Joy Dunne each found the back of the net in the third to put the game away. The U.S. outshot Germany 38-13. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Wendell Cruz The NHL’s Department of Player Safety announced Sunday that New York Islanders defenseman Logan Stanley has been fined $3,865 for slashing New Jersey Devils forward Nico Hischier. The fine was the maximum allowable under the collective bargaining agreement. The incident occurred during the Devils’ 5-4 overtime win against the Islanders. While the two players stood in front of the New York net, Stanley took several massive whacks at Hischier, which left him sprawled on the ice before a scrum ensued in front of the net. In 10 NHL seasons, the New Jersey captain has 206 goals and 293 assists for 499 points in 626 career regular-season games. items.body: Logan Stanley is facing some discipline after a net-front tussle. The New York Islanders defenceman has been fined $3,865.98, the maximum amount allowable under the collective bargaining agreement, for slashing New Jersey Devils forward Nico Hischier , the NHL's department of player safety announced Sunday. The incident occurred in the second period of Saturday's 5-4 Devils overtime win. Near the end of the frame, Stanley laid into the net-front Hischier, forcing the Devils captain onto the ice. As Hischier got up, he poked at Stanley, to which the Islanders defenceman retaliated with a hard slash, sending Hischier to the ice once more, then pushed him while he was already down. The two players then exchanged some words and a scrum ensued after play was called dead. Stanley received two minor penalties on the play — one for the slash and another for roughing as part of the scrum. The 28-year-old Kitchener, Ont., native leads the Islanders in penalty minutes with 34 in his first year with the team. He also had five assists in 16 games.

items.summary: The Washington Capitals’ Tom Wilson won’t face further discipline after his actions on Saturday night.
items.body: The Washington Capitals ' Tom Wilson won't face further discipline after his actions on Saturday. Wilson delivered a hard hit to the back of Florida Panthers ' Sandis Vilmanis in the first period that sent the forward headfirst into the area where the glass meets the boards. Vilmanis left the game and did not return, and Wilson received a major penalty for boarding and a game misconduct for the play. After speculation about whether Wilson would face a hearing for the hit, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported Sunday that he's hearing the Capitals' star will not face supplemental discipline. Panthers coach Paul Maurice said after the game that Florida was waiting on more information about Vilmanis' condition. “Getting looked at by another doctor tomorrow," he said. "But probably we’ll have to wait until we get him back to see our guys before we have a real good idea, get some imaging.” Wilson has been suspended several times during his 14-year career. He was given 20 games for a blindside hit to the head in 2018, a ban later reduced to 14 games on appeal after he had already served 16. He received a seven-game suspension for boarding Boston’s Brandon Carlo with head contact in 2021 and six games in 2024 for a stick to the face of Toronto Maple Leafs forward Noah Gregor. The 22-year-old Vilmanis had his first career two-goal game Wednesday night when Florida beat Chicago.

items.summary: Defenceman Kevin Bahl is set to undergo season-ending surgery to repair a ruptured Achilles tendon, the team announced Sunday.
items.body: The Calgary Flames have lost a piece on their blue line for the remainder of the year. Defenceman Kevin Bahl is set to undergo season-ending surgery to repair a ruptured Achilles tendon, the team announced Sunday. "A terrible break for a guy that I would consider our best player up to this point in the season," head coach Ryan Huska said of Bahl's injury. "Unfortunately, sometimes things happen, and because of that, we're losing a really good player for the rest of the year." Bahl suffered the injury on Friday prior to warmups ahead of the game against the Anaheim Ducks and was promptly ruled out. Joel Hanley entered the lineup in his place. The 26-year-old had played in all 16 of Calgary's games this season, averaging 21:56 of ice time per night while collecting one goal and one assist. Playing in his seventh NHL season, the New Westminster, B.C., native has picked up 12 goals and 53 assists in 313 games split between the Flames and New Jersey Devils. Bahl was acquired by the Flames in 2024 as part of the trade that sent Jacob Markstrom to New Jersey.

Devin Cooley is set to make his return to the Calgary Flames ' crease for Sunday's showdown against the Philadelphia Flyers (Sportsnet West, 7 p.m. ET / 6 p.m. ABT), the team announced after morning skate. Cooley hasn't started for the Flames since a game against the Edmonton Oilers on Oct. 28. He exited that game in the first period with a lower-body injury and was placed on the injured list. The 29-year-old was activated earlier this week, but Dustin Wolf got the nod for the Flames' last game against the Anaheim Ducks on Friday. He had been red-hot before he went down injured, allowing just six goals on 133 shots over his previous four starts. In another move, the Flames recalled defenceman Brayden Pachal from the AHL Wranglers. Pachal, 27, has yet to skate for the Flames this season, but has three assists in 11 games with the Wranglers. The Estevan, Sask., native has six goals and 22 assists in 177 games over five seasons at the NHL level. He had a career-best three goals and nine assists in 76 games with the Flames last year. Heading into Sunday's action, the Flames are fifth in the Pacific Division with a 7-9-1 record but have lost two straight.

items.body: It’s early November and the Chicago Blackhawks are in a familiar spot. Second-to-last in the NHL, with a league-worst minus-37 goal differential and barreling through another season that feels destined to be lost. The pain of a rebuild is usually a small price to pay for three Stanley Cups from Chicago’s previous core, but this one has been particularly agonizing. The Blackhawks have missed the playoffs six years in a row and appear headed for a seventh. There also doesn’t seem to be many positive signs to build on going forward. Sure, Connor Bedard looks every bit of a superstar in the making, though there aren’t many running mates who are going to help the Blackhawks captain imminently. items.summary: Crosby recorded his 1,772nd career point and passed Marcel Dionne for sixth on the NHL’s all-time list.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Sidney Crosby moved into sole possession of sixth place on the NHL’s all-time points list after he scored twice to help the Pittsburgh Penguins win 5-2 over the Los Angeles Kings Saturday night. Crosby passed Hockey Hall of Famer Marcel Dionne with his 1,772nd point after he deflected the puck past Kings goaltender Darcy Kuemper in the second period. He scored an empty netter to seal the win for Pittsburgh. The 39-year-old now has six goals and six assists for 12 points in 17 games this season. In 2025-26, Crosby passed Mario Lemieux and Steve Yzerman for eighth and seventh all-time in points, respectively. He now needs 26 points to pass Hall of Famer Ron Francis for fifth on the all-time list. Across 21 NHL seasons, Crosby has 660 goals and 1,113 assists for 1,773 points in 1,437 career regular-season games. He has hit the 100-point mark in six seasons and recorded at least 50 assists in a season 12 times. During that time, he’s broken the 100-point mark six times, recorded at least 50 assists 12 times, hit the 30-goal mark 13 times and has averaged more than a point-per-game in every season of his career. Crosby also has 72 goals and 134 assists for 206 points in 186 career playoff games. He captained the Penguins to three Stanley Cup championships in 2009, 2016 and 2017, and helped them reach the Stanley Cup Final in 2008. He also won the Conn Smythe Trophy in both 2016 and 2017. Crosby has twice won each of the Hart Trophy, the Art Ross Trophy, the Maurice “Rocket” Richard Trophy and the Ted Lindsay Award.

items.body: Explanation: The play on the ice was challenged under Rule 38 – Coach’s Challenge. Rule 38.1 states, “In all Coach’s Challenge situations, the original call on the ice will be overturned if, and only if, a conclusive and irrefutable determination can be made on the basis of video evidence that the original call on the ice was clearly not correct. If a review is not conclusive and/or there is any doubt whatsoever as to whether the call on the ice was correct, the original call on the ice will be confirmed.” Video review determined that Los Angeles’ Alex Laferriere preceded the puck into the offensive zone and was in an off-side position prior to the goal. According to Rule 38.9, “The standard for overturning the call in the event of a “GOAL” call on the ice is that the NHL Situation Room, after reviewing any and all available replays and consulting with the On-Ice Official(s), determines that one or more Players on the attacking team preceded the puck into the attacking zone prior to the goal being scored and that, as a result, the play should have been stopped for an “Off-Side” infraction; where this standard is met, the goal will be disallowed.” The clock is reset to show 4:29 (15:31 elapsed time), when the off-side infraction occurred.

items.body: EDMONTON — Leon Draisaitl had two goals and an assist and Connor McDavid added three assists as the Edmonton Oilers came away with a 4-2 victory over the struggling Vancouver Canucks on Saturday. Mattias Ekholm and Jason Dickinson also scored for the Oilers (12-3-3) who snapped a two-game losing skid. The Oilers are 10-0-2 when they score first this season. Devon Levi returned from injury to record 20 saves and improve to 7-1-0 in the Edmonton net. Max Sasson and Brock Boeser replied for the Canucks (3-15-1) who have lost five straight and 15 of their last 16. Canucks: Swedish forward Liam Öhgren was unable to extend his scoring streak to three games. The 22-year-old had scored four goals in his previous five games, including his first-ever power-play goal. Oilers: McDavid extended his season-starting points and assists streak to 18 games. He now leads the league with 10 goals, 37 assists and 47 points. The Oilers captain matched Adam Oates for the second-longest assist streak in NHL history behind only Wayne Gretzky’s 23 games set in 1990-91. McDavid also became the sixth player in NHL history with a season-opening 18-game point streak. Edmonton took a 3-1 lead four minutes into the final frame as their potent power play struck when McDavid sent it across to Draisaitl and he unleashed his patented one-timer for his 15th of the season. Evan Bouchard extended his points streak to six games and both he and Draisaitl have points in 16 of 18 games. The Canucks came into the game sporting a dreadful minus-30 goal differential, a staggering 4.61 goals against per game. Meanwhile, the Oilers came in as the league’s highest-scoring team, averaging 4.12 goals per contest.

items.body: Register Login Evening Notes: Willander, Rielly, Byram By Gabriel Foley | at November 7, 2026 9:21 pm The Vancouver Canucks took to warmups without defenseman Tom Willander ahead of Saturday’s game against the Edmonton Oilers. He will miss a third straight game after sitting out of the last two with a lower-body injury sustained on Tuesday. This update should keep Guillaume Brisebois in the lineup. Willander’s absence will continue to weigh on the Canucks blue-line. The second-year pro is the only Canucks defenseman without a negative plus-minus. He has recorded three assists, four penalty minutes, 10 hits, and 17 shot blocks in 16 games so far. He’s yet to find a scoring groove after a 21-point rookie season – but is on pace for more shots (63), hits (53), and blocks (89) than last season. More than that, Willander is facing much tougher competition. He has averaged 20 minutes of ice time a night and played a career-high 25:43 on October 13th. Willander is an evolving piece of the Canucks’ defense. His next chance to return to the lineup will be Monday’s matchup against the Philadelphia Flyers.

items.title: Jack Hughes scores in overtime as Devils rally past Islanders
items.body: NEW YORK — Jack Hughes scored in overtime to lift the New Jersey Devils to a 5-4 victory over the New York Islanders on Saturday. Dougie Hamilton, Luke Evangelista, Declan Chisholm and Evan Rodrigues also scored for New Jersey, which extended its winning streak to four games. Jake Allen made 19 saves. Hughes scored with 3:42 remaining in overtime, keeping the puck on a two-on-one rush before firing a shot past Ilya Sorokin’s blocker. Anthony Duclair, Matthew Schaefer, Simon Holmstrom and Victor Eklund scored for New York, which lost its third straight game. Sorokin finished with 45 saves and captain Bo Horvat added two assists. The Devils erased a two-goal deficit in the third period, capped by Hamilton’s power-play goal with 6:18 remaining in regulation. Jack Hughes curled around the net before finding Hamilton in the slot for the tying goal. Evangelista started the comeback when he pulled New Jersey within a goal at 6:08 of the third period. The Islanders took a 2-1 lead after the first period. Duclair opened the scoring with less than five minutes remaining, Rodrigues tied it 17 seconds later and Schaefer put New York back ahead with his fifth goal of the season. Chisholm tied the score at 2 just 4:42 into the second period when Jesper Bratt fired a shot off the end boards that took an awkward bounce around the net, allowing Chisholm to bury the rebound. Two of Islanders goaltender Ilya Sorokin’s best saves came against Devils captain Nico Hischier. Sorokin denied Hischier on a breakaway in the closing seconds of the second period and stopped a one-timer in the opening minute of the third.

items.title: Ref appears to offer Canadiens’ Fowler an apple
items.summary: An apple nearly took a bite out of Montreal Canadiens goaltender Jacob Fowler on Saturday.
items.body: An apple nearly took a bite out of Montreal Canadiens goaltender Jacob Fowler on Saturday. The apple found its way to the ice during the second period of a game between the Canadiens and Maple Leafs in Toronto. Referee TJ Luxmore was seen on camera holding it up to Fowler before disposing of it. Fowler told Sportsnet's Kyle Bukauskas after the game that the apple wasn't real but added that it was still one of the weirdest things he'd ever seen hit the ice. "I was pretty dialled in but I saw an apple come on the ice right in front of me. I'm used to tracking a black puck not a green apple," Fowler said with a laugh. "I saw that one and (Luxmore) told me he would have blown the play dead if they had gotten in the zone so thankfully they didn't get one there." The flying apple didn't faze Fowler, who stopped 26 saves in a 4-2 win.
